nodes.label: Entanglement ablation (basic.cfg)

nodes.label: Hand-crafted angle features (depth + labels buffers)

nodes.label: Known issues
nodes.rationale: PPO loop copied across three scripts; joint grad clipping lets critic dominate norm; per-step reward metric is noisy; timeouts marked terminated in older envs; non-monsters treated as enemies; final RZ gates redundant; depth normalisation saturates ~38 units

nodes.label: My Way Home scenario
nodes.rationale: Quantum agent 14/20 greedy vs random 2/20; qubit 9 proximity uses true goal distance, not vision

nodes.label: Quantum-only policy and value model
nodes.rationale: 12 qubits, 2 re-uploading layers; 7 Pauli-Z expectations as action logits, 8th as value; no classical MLP or learned linear readout; scalar gains only

nodes.label: Redundant final-layer RZ gates
nodes.rationale: RZ before Z measurement has no effect, so 8-12 parameters are redundant

nodes.label: Finding: all 5 seeds follow the waypoint route to the exit room
nodes.norm_label: finding: all 5 seeds follow the waypoint route to the exit room
nodes.rationale: All five seed trajectories closely track the dashed waypoint route from START through doors at wp5 and wp16-17 down to the final exit room (wp20-21); trajectories diverge little, suggesting a consistent route-following policy or scripted route check. Some seeds (0,2) wander inside the exit room near the green exit line, so whether exit was actually triggered is AMBIGUOUS.

nodes.label: Route Structure Finding
nodes.rationale: Route goes north from start through door at waypoint 5 into the upper room, east across to waypoint 10, then south through a monster-occupied zigzag area (monsters near waypoints 11, 15, 18) and doors at waypoints 16, 17, 20 to the exit at waypoint 21; doors and monsters on-path are the key obstacles for an RL agent.

nodes.label: Finding: Reward Rises ~0.05 to ~0.3
nodes.rationale: Over ~128 PPO updates, smoothed mean step reward climbs from ~0.05 to ~0.3-0.4 (peak ~0.41 near update 92 and 111), showing the quantum policy learns to navigate, though raw values are highly noisy.

nodes.label: Finding: Success Rate Improves but Volatile
nodes.norm_label: finding: success rate improves but volatile
nodes.rationale: Goal success rate oscillates wildly (0-100%) early, then mostly settles in ~40-85% range after update ~65, ending ~64%; small per-update episode counts likely cause the spikes (AMBIGUOUS inference).

nodes.label: Ablation Curve: Entangled PQC vs Unentangled vs Classical MLP (ViZDoom Aiming & Combat)
nodes.norm_label: ablation curve: entangled pqc vs unentangled vs classical mlp (vizdoom aiming & combat)

nodes.label: Finding: classical MLP still outperforms entangled PQC
nodes.norm_label: finding: classical mlp still outperforms entangled pqc
nodes.rationale: The classical MLP learns fastest and reaches ~10-10.5 mean step reward vs ~8.4 for the entangled PQC at update 31; the gap narrows late in training but the quantum model does not surpass the classical baseline in this run (single run, no error bars shown).

nodes.label: Finding: entanglement is necessary for PQC learning
nodes.norm_label: finding: entanglement is necessary for pqc learning
nodes.rationale: Over 32 PPO updates (~32k frames), the entangled PQC rises from ~-2.3 to ~8.4 mean step reward, while the unentangled product-state PQC stays flat near -4 (ending ~-1.7). Removing entanglement essentially kills learning, so entangling gates contribute the representational power.

nodes.label: Finding: All 5 Seeds Follow Route to Exit
nodes.norm_label: finding: all 5 seeds follow route to exit
nodes.rationale: All five seed trajectories closely track the 22-waypoint reference route from START through the north room, down the east corridor, through doors to the exit room; minor jitter/backtracking near waypoints 10-11, 16-17 and in the exit room (wiggle around waypoint 21). Success per seed inferred from trajectories ending at exit room.

nodes.label: PPO Update
nodes.rationale: x-axis is PPO update index (0 to ~255); agent trained with Proximal Policy Optimization

nodes.label: Fast Convergence then Plateau at ~60
nodes.rationale: Mean step reward rises from ~5 to ~57 within ~35 PPO updates, then plateaus around 58-62 for the remaining ~220 updates with +/-5 noise; no further improvement or collapse, suggesting the 8-qubit PQC policy converges quickly but saturates (possible capacity limit or local optimum).

nodes.label: Empty Input-Angle Plot Finding
nodes.rationale: The 12-qubit input angle panel shows axes (x 0-11, y -pi..pi) but no plotted data points, suggesting the encoded angles were not rendered (possibly NaN, out-of-range, or a plotting bug) at the time of this sanity check.

nodes.label: Sanity Check Figure (Frame -> Label Buffer -> 8-Qubit Angles)
nodes.norm_label: sanity check figure (frame -> label buffer -> 8-qubit angles)

nodes.label: Monster Detected in Sectors 4-5
nodes.rationale: Monster sits slightly right of center (x~200 of 320) in RGB frame and label buffer; qubits 4 and 5 receive positive angles (~+1.5 rad, ~pi/2) while all other sectors get small negative angles (~-0.4 to -0.65), confirming the label-buffer-to-angle encoding localizes the enemy correctly. Exact angle values AMBIGUOUS (read from bar heights).

nodes.label: Zero-CNN Feature Extraction
nodes.rationale: Uses ViZDoom's native label buffer for object segmentation instead of a learned CNN, so a small 8-qubit circuit can receive compact, semantically meaningful inputs. Note: label buffer is privileged info relative to human-equivalent screen-only observation (INFERRED tension with project constraint).

nodes.label: Auxiliary depth and goal-visibility losses
nodes.rationale: Training-only linear head predicts per-sector log depth and goal visibility; goal pixels ~1% of sectors so pos_weight=20; targets never policy inputs

nodes.label: Matched classical vs bridged-quantum comparison
nodes.rationale: Neither distinguishable from random (Fisher p~0.6); seed 20017 accounts for most successes; fixed RGB sector summaries and budget more likely bottleneck than policy model

nodes.label: Memory bridges (controlled rotations)
nodes.rationale: Trainable controlled rotations from each memory qubit to every action/value readout raise turn-logit sensitivity to memory features, which was near zero in the original circuit

nodes.label: Private progress and kill rewards
nodes.rationale: Potential-based reward from distance change to endpoint plus kill bonus; privileged info used only in reward, never policy input; did not improve held-out item collection

nodes.label: RGB place memory (VisualPlaceMemory)
nodes.rationale: Augments travel grid with RGB keyframes, visual revisit matching and links between cells; still reads no engine pose

nodes.label: Screen-only navigation memory experiment
nodes.rationale: Policy sees only RGB-derived features plus optional 4-value travel map from action odometry; no reliable memory benefit over 20 episodes; map drifts without place recognition and RGB sector compression discards much of the image

nodes.label: Human-visible observation constraint
nodes.rationale: Policy must not read engine position, depth, labels, objects, goal coordinates or WAD map; only screen-derived input (with privileged training feedback via reward)

nodes.label: E1M1 12-qubit observation
nodes.rationale: Qubits 0-7 FOV sectors, 8 bearing to waypoint/exit, 9 waypoint proximity, 10 health, 11 door/exit ahead; reward: waypoint progress, damage -0.05/HP, kill +2, death -50, exit +100; timeouts returned as truncated

nodes.label: Reverse-start curriculum
nodes.rationale: Starts at waypoints 21,20,19,16,12,6 then true start; advances after >=3 exits in latest 20 episodes; chosen because scripted exits succeed from waypoint 19/16 but warping to door waypoint 17 stalls; neither fixed nor adaptive run completed E1M1

nodes.label: Route planner (grid Dijkstra)
nodes.rationale: 16-unit grid, blocks walls within player radius, step-ups >24, gaps <56; penalises nukage; boolean-mask bug once produced a route through a wall; corrected route 22 waypoints ~4972 units

nodes.label: Route validation (scripted follower)
nodes.rationale: Gate: training checks for at least one skill-3 exit before spending GPU time

nodes.label: Success-detection bug
nodes.rationale: Vest +1 reward can land before episode end so raw_reward > 0 missed pickups; fixed with get_total_reward() > 0.5 in HumanNavigationEnv and PixelNavigationEnv; doom_nav_env.py still uses old test

nodes.label: 12-qubit circuit head result (96/100)
nodes.rationale: Circuit head reaches vest from screen alone on 96/100 unseen spawns vs classical 99-100; ~9x slower; CNN does most perception so this shows trainability, not circuit contribution; needs linear-readout control and more seeds

nodes.label: Learned screen encoder (CNN to 12-value bottleneck)
nodes.rationale: Four stacked 80x60 RGB screens with HUD through small CNN into 12 values in [-pi,pi]; identical encoder for classical and circuit heads so the head is the only variable
